import unittest
import support_address as app

class Behavior(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_local_case_preserved(self):
        self.assertEqual(app.normalize_address('HelpDesk@EXAMPLE.COM'), 'HelpDesk@example.com')
        self.assertEqual(app.normalize_address('A.B+Tag@MAIL.Example.ORG'), 'A.B+Tag@mail.example.org')
        self.assertEqual(app.normalize_address('MiXeD@x'), 'MiXeD@x')
    def test_whitespace_and_idempotence(self):
        self.assertEqual(app.normalize_address(' \tOrders@Example.Com\n'), 'Orders@example.com')
        self.assertEqual(app.normalize_address('ready@example.com'), 'ready@example.com')
        normalized = app.normalize_address('ApiKey@HOST.ORG')
        self.assertEqual(app.normalize_address(normalized), normalized)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

# support-address-domain

Behavior contract:
normalize_address(address) strips surrounding whitespace and lowercases only the domain after '@', preserving the local part before '@' exactly. Input is an ASCII address with exactly one '@' and nonempty parts. Return a string; invalid-address validation is not required.

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.
Use only the Python 3.12 standard library. Keep the interface and leave tests/ unchanged.
